subtopic_detail: Sequencing drug withdrawal before adding an antipsychotic in Parkinson disease psychosis
stem:
You are the general medicine registrar reviewing a 74 year old man with Parkinson disease of eight years duration in the movement disorder clinic. His wife says that for six weeks he has been seeing cats and small children in the hallway in the evenings, and that last week he began accusing her of hiding money from him.

He takes levodopa with carbidopa four times daily and ropinirole, which was added six months ago for end of dose wearing off. His conscious state is clear and steady through the day, his attention is intact and his memory and conversation are unchanged from six months ago. He has no urinary symptoms, no cough and no constipation.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 74 beats per minute, blood pressure 128/72 mmHg lying and 112/66 mmHg standing, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, SpO2 97 per cent on room air, temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius
data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, electrolytes, calcium, liver function tests, thyroid stimulating hormone, urinalysis and chest radiograph all within normal limits
data_table.Cognitive assessment: Montreal Cognitive Assessment 25 out of 30, unchanged from six months ago

lead_in: What is the most appropriate first step?

options.text: Reduce and cease ropinirole while continuing levodopa with carbidopa
options.rationale: Once delirium is excluded, the first step is to withdraw the antiparkinsonian drug most likely to be responsible, and dopamine agonists carry a far higher risk of hallucinations and delusions than levodopa while contributing less to motor benefit (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology; Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Commence risperidone 0.5 mg at night and continue current therapy
options.rationale: Risperidone blocks striatal dopamine receptors and reliably worsens parkinsonism, and adding any antipsychotic before rationalising the antiparkinsonian regimen inverts the recommended order (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Commence olanzapine 2.5 mg at night and continue current therapy
options.rationale: Olanzapine has been shown to worsen motor function in Parkinson disease without improving psychosis, and quetiapine or clozapine are the only antipsychotics used in this population once drug reduction has failed (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Commence haloperidol 0.5 mg as required and review in one week
options.rationale: A high potency typical antipsychotic can precipitate severe rigidity and immobility in Parkinson disease and is contraindicated in this setting (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Increase the levodopa with carbidopa dose and review in one week
options.rationale: Increasing dopaminergic load worsens psychotic symptoms, and the near pair distinction is that levodopa is the drug retained for motor benefit while the agonist is the one withdrawn (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

explanation.summary: Psychosis affects up to half of people with Parkinson disease over the course of the illness and is the strongest single predictor of residential care admission. Management follows a fixed order: exclude delirium from infection, metabolic derangement or a new drug, then withdraw antiparkinsonian drugs from the least useful to the most useful, and only then add an antipsychotic. The usual withdrawal sequence is anticholinergics, then amantadine, then dopamine agonists, then catechol O methyltransferase and monoamine oxidase B inhibitors, leaving levodopa last because it carries the best ratio of motor benefit to psychiatric risk. When drug reduction fails or motor function cannot tolerate it, quetiapine is used first and clozapine has the strongest evidence, with pimavanserin unavailable in Australia.
key_points: Exclude delirium before attributing hallucinations to Parkinson disease psychosis
Withdraw dopamine agonists before reducing levodopa
Risperidone, olanzapine and haloperidol all worsen parkinsonism
Quetiapine then clozapine are the antipsychotics used if drug reduction fails
Preserved attention and a stable conscious state argue against delirium
explanation.pearls: Clozapine at doses as low as 12.5 to 50 mg at night improves Parkinson disease psychosis without worsening motor function, but it still requires the full haematological monitoring protocol, which is why quetiapine is usually tried first.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

subtopic_detail: Antidepressant selection where a cytochrome interaction would reduce the efficacy of cancer therapy
stem:
You are the general practitioner seeing a 52 year old woman eight months into tamoxifen 20 mg daily for an oestrogen receptor positive breast cancer. For the past three months she has had low mood most of the day, has stopped seeing friends, wakes at four each morning and has lost interest in work she used to enjoy.

She also describes drenching hot flushes about ten times a day that disturb her sleep. She has no suicidal thoughts, no past psychiatric history and no history of mania. She takes no other regular medication and her ECG shows a corrected QT interval of 418 ms.

data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, electrolytes, liver function tests and thyroid stimulating hormone within normal limits

lead_in: Which antidepressant is the most appropriate choice?

options.text: Commence paroxetine 20 mg daily and review in four weeks
options.rationale: Paroxetine is the most potent cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibitor among the antidepressants and blocks conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite endoxifen, which has been associated with increased breast cancer mortality (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook; eviQ).

options.text: Commence fluoxetine 20 mg daily and review in four weeks
options.rationale: Fluoxetine is also a strong cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibitor and its long half life means the interaction persists for weeks after it is stopped (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Commence bupropion 150 mg daily and review in four weeks
options.rationale: Bupropion is a strong cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibitor despite not being a serotonergic drug, so its different mechanism does not make it a safe alternative here (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Commence venlafaxine 75 mg daily and review in four weeks
options.rationale: Venlafaxine has minimal effect on cytochrome P450 2D6 and is the preferred antidepressant during tamoxifen therapy, with the additional benefit that serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors reduce vasomotor symptoms (Source: eviQ; Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Commence duloxetine 60 mg daily and review in four weeks
options.rationale: Duloxetine is a moderate cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibitor, so within the same drug class venlafaxine is preferred when tamoxifen is being taken (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Tamoxifen is a prodrug that requires cytochrome P450 2D6 to be converted to endoxifen, the metabolite responsible for most of its antioestrogen effect. Drugs that inhibit this enzyme lower endoxifen concentrations substantially, and observational data link strong inhibitors to worse breast cancer outcomes, so Australian oncology guidance advises avoiding them for the whole duration of tamoxifen therapy. Depression and vasomotor symptoms are both common in this group, and a serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor addresses each, which is why venlafaxine has become the default. Where a strong inhibitor is unavoidable, switching to an aromatase inhibitor in a postmenopausal woman removes the interaction entirely because that class does not require metabolic activation.
key_points: Tamoxifen requires cytochrome P450 2D6 activation to endoxifen
Paroxetine, fluoxetine and bupropion are strong inhibitors of this enzyme
Venlafaxine and escitalopram have minimal effect on the enzyme
Serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors also reduce hot flushes
Switching to an aromatase inhibitor removes the interaction in postmenopausal women
explanation.pearls: Venlafaxine 37.5 to 75 mg daily reduces hot flush frequency by around 60 per cent within four weeks, which makes it the single most useful antidepressant choice for a woman with both depression and vasomotor symptoms on tamoxifen.

subtopic_detail: Managing lithium toxicity precipitated by a newly added antihypertensive
stem:
You are the emergency registrar seeing a 58 year old man with bipolar affective disorder who has taken lithium carbonate 900 mg at night for nine years with concentrations consistently between 0.6 and 0.8 mmol/L. His wife says that for four days he has been vomiting, his hands have been shaking badly enough to spill his drink, and he has been walking as if he were drunk.

His general practitioner started a tablet for blood pressure three weeks ago. He is alert and orientated with slurred speech, a coarse tremor of both hands and a broad based unsteady gait. There is no fever, no rigidity, no clonus and no seizure activity.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 92 beats per minute, blood pressure 118/70 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, SpO2 98 per cent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius
data_table.Investigations: Serum lithium 1.9 mmol/L (0.6-0.8), creatinine 132 micromol/L (60-110), estimated glomerular filtration rate 48 mL/min/1.73m2, sodium 133 mmol/L (135-145), potassium 3.3 mmol/L (3.5-5.2)
data_table.Medications: Lithium carbonate 900 mg at night, indapamide 2.5 mg daily started three weeks ago

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Arrange urgent haemodialysis and cease all regular medication
options.rationale: Haemodialysis is indicated for a concentration above 4.0 mmol/L, or above 2.5 mmol/L with seizures, a depressed conscious state or failing renal function, and none of those thresholds is met (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Toxicology and Toxinology).

options.text: Cease lithium and indapamide and give intravenous sodium chloride
options.rationale: Thiazide type diuretics increase proximal tubular reabsorption of lithium and precipitate toxicity, so both drugs are stopped and volume is restored with isotonic saline to promote renal lithium excretion (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Toxicology and Toxinology; Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Halve the lithium dose and recheck the concentration in one week
options.rationale: Continuing any lithium in a symptomatic patient with impaired clearance allows the concentration to keep rising, and a week is far too long an interval for a toxic patient (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Give activated charcoal 50 g and observe on the ward overnight
options.rationale: Charcoal does not adsorb lithium because it is a small inorganic cation, which distinguishes it from most drug overdoses where charcoal has a role (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Toxicology and Toxinology).

options.text: Continue lithium at a reduced dose and cease indapamide only
options.rationale: Removing the interacting drug alone leaves the patient exposed while renal function recovers, and the concentration will not fall quickly enough to relieve the neurological features (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Lithium is handled by the kidney like sodium, so anything that reduces effective circulating volume or increases proximal tubular sodium reabsorption raises the concentration. The classic culprits are thiazide and thiazide like diuretics, angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers and non steroidal anti inflammatory drugs, along with dehydration from any cause. Chronic toxicity produces predominantly neurological features at concentrations that would be tolerated in acute overdose, because tissue distribution has already occurred, so the concentration correlates poorly with severity. The persistent risk is the syndrome of irreversible lithium effectuated neurotoxicity, in which cerebellar signs persist after the concentration normalises, which is why prompt cessation and volume repletion matter more than the absolute number.
key_points: Thiazides, angiotensin blocking drugs and non steroidal anti inflammatory drugs precipitate toxicity
Chronic toxicity causes neurological features at lower concentrations than acute overdose
Isotonic saline restores volume and promotes renal lithium excretion
Activated charcoal does not bind lithium
Dialysis thresholds are above 4.0 mmol/L, or above 2.5 mmol/L with severe features
explanation.pearls: Recheck the serum lithium every six hours during treatment of chronic toxicity, because redistribution from tissue stores can produce a rebound rise after an initial fall and change the decision about dialysis.

subtopic_detail: Oral supplementation requirements when initiating a long acting injectable antipsychotic
stem:
You are the psychiatry registrar in a community mental health team seeing a 26 year old man with schizophrenia who has been well on oral aripiprazole 15 mg daily for four months after a relapse that followed several weeks of missed tablets. He works shift work and tells you he forgets his morning dose whenever his roster changes.

He has agreed to a monthly injection of the same drug and has never received a long acting injectable before. He has no extrapyramidal signs, his weight and metabolic screen are stable, and his last relapse resolved fully on oral treatment.

data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, electrolytes, liver function tests, fasting glucose, lipids and prolactin within normal limits
data_table.Electrocardiogram: Sinus rhythm with a corrected QT interval of 402 ms

lead_in: How should the first injection be managed?

options.text: Give the injection and cease oral aripiprazole on the same day
options.rationale: Aripiprazole monohydrate reaches therapeutic plasma concentrations slowly, so stopping the oral drug at the first injection leaves a two week window of subtherapeutic cover and relapse risk (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Give the injection and continue oral aripiprazole for three days
options.rationale: Three days of overlap is the pattern used for some other long acting injectables and is far too short for aripiprazole monohydrate, whose absorption from the depot is slow (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Give the injection and continue oral aripiprazole for fourteen days
options.rationale: The approved initiation for aripiprazole monohydrate is a first injection with 14 consecutive days of concurrent oral aripiprazole, which covers the interval before depot concentrations become therapeutic (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook; Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Give the injection and repeat a second loading dose after one week
options.rationale: A second injection one week after the first is the loading pattern used for paliperidone palmitate, and applying it to aripiprazole risks accumulation without providing early cover (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Give the injection and start oral olanzapine cover for fourteen days
options.rationale: Cover should be with the same drug already established as effective and tolerated, and introducing a second antipsychotic adds metabolic and sedative burden without benefit (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

explanation.summary: Long acting injectable antipsychotics reduce relapse and rehospitalisation in schizophrenia and are particularly useful where adherence is the limiting factor rather than efficacy. Each product has its own initiation requirement, and confusing them is a common prescribing error: aripiprazole monohydrate needs 14 days of oral overlap, paliperidone palmitate uses a two injection deltoid loading schedule at day one and day eight with no oral cover, and risperidone microspheres need three weeks of oral cover because release does not begin for 21 days. Establishing tolerability on the oral form first is standard before any injectable is given. Site, needle length and the difference between deltoid and gluteal absorption also matter, and the patient should be told that a missed injection is managed differently from a missed tablet.
key_points: Aripiprazole monohydrate requires 14 days of concurrent oral aripiprazole
Paliperidone palmitate uses day one and day eight loading with no oral cover
Risperidone microspheres require three weeks of oral cover
Establish oral tolerability before any long acting injectable is commenced
Cover with the same drug rather than introducing a second antipsychotic
explanation.pearls: If a patient established on monthly aripiprazole monohydrate misses an injection by more than five weeks but less than six weeks, the next dose is given with seven days of oral aripiprazole cover rather than the full 14 day schedule used at initiation.

subtopic_detail: Distinguishing a movement side effect from worsening psychosis in an inpatient
stem:
You are the psychiatry registrar reviewing a 23 year old man admitted three weeks ago with a first episode of psychosis and started on olanzapine 15 mg at night. The voices that frightened him on admission have almost gone and he no longer believes his flatmates are recording him.

Over the past five days he has been pacing the corridor for hours and cannot stay seated through a meal. He tells you his legs feel like they have to keep moving and that this is worse than the voices ever were. There is no rigidity, no tremor, no fever and no diaphoresis, and the nursing staff have asked whether the dose should be increased.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 96 beats per minute, blood pressure 124/74 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, SpO2 98 per cent on room air, temperature 36.9 degrees Celsius
data_table.Investigations: Creatine kinase 118 U/L (40-320), full blood count, electrolytes, liver function tests and thyroid stimulating hormone within normal limits
data_table.Examination: Constant shifting of weight from foot to foot when standing and rocking when seated, with normal tone and no cogwheeling

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Increase olanzapine to 20 mg daily to target residual psychosis
options.rationale: Increasing the antipsychotic is the specific trap because the restlessness is dose related, and escalating worsens it while the psychotic symptoms are already resolving (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Commence benztropine 2 mg twice daily and review in one week
options.rationale: Anticholinergics relieve drug induced parkinsonism and acute dystonia but are ineffective for this syndrome, and they add cognitive impairment, constipation and urinary retention (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Commence lorazepam 1 mg three times daily and review in a week
options.rationale: A benzodiazepine is a reasonable second line addition but does not address the dose related cause, and regular use in a young man with a new psychotic illness risks dependence (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Commence sodium valproate 500 mg twice daily for the agitation
options.rationale: Valproate treats agitation arising from mood elevation rather than a movement side effect, and it would add weight gain to an antipsychotic that already causes it (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Reduce the olanzapine dose and commence propranolol 10 mg daily
options.rationale: The subjective urge to move with objective restlessness and no rigidity is akathisia, managed first by reducing the antipsychotic dose and adding a lipophilic beta blocker such as propranolol (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic; Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

explanation.summary: Akathisia is among the most distressing antipsychotic adverse effects and is independently associated with suicidal thinking and with treatment refusal, so recognising it changes outcomes rather than merely comfort. Its defining feature is the subjective inner restlessness, which distinguishes it from psychomotor agitation driven by psychosis and from drug induced parkinsonism where tone is increased. The commonest error is to read the pacing as worsening illness and to increase the antipsychotic, which produces a rapid deterioration. Management is dose reduction or a switch to a lower risk agent, with propranolol as the best supported adjunct and a benzodiazepine or mirtazapine used when a beta blocker is contraindicated or ineffective.
key_points: The subjective urge to move is what defines akathisia
Normal tone and normal creatine kinase separate it from parkinsonism and malignant syndrome
Reduce the antipsychotic dose before adding any adjunct
Anticholinergics do not help akathisia
Akathisia is independently associated with suicidal ideation
explanation.pearls: Propranolol 10 to 20 mg two or three times daily usually improves akathisia within days, and its lipophilicity matters because water soluble beta blockers such as atenolol do not cross the blood brain barrier well enough to work.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
